utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Call the case, please, Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. This is the case number IT-98-34-T, the Prosecutor versus Naletilic and Martinovic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Meek.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: Good morning, Mr. President and Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: Cross-examined by Mr. Meek:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Good morning, LL. How are you this morning?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS LL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Very well, thank you. Although I speak only French and Spanish, I can understand and be understood by the whole world, and I am very happy about that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: LL, I wish I were so lucky. I think we left off yesterday -- you were explaining that in your life, you feel that being sincere with a person helps to gain their trust and that you believe people when you speak with them; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS LL [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is right.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness LL, in being sincere with somebody, would that also compass the notion of being honest with that person?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS LL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness LL, do you tape-record the conversations of all your conversations with your friends?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS LL [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you did tape the conversation of the evening of the dinner party with Ivan Andabak, Mr. Tuta, General Zorzo and the others at Mr. Andabak's house, did you not?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS LL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And is it your testimony that you tape-record all conversations you have with friends?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS LL [Resumed]
utterances.text: When I am working for the military, then it is regular for me so as to be able to understand better the problems and aspects of the social life of people with whom I am in contact with so as to understand better what could be their problems and how can I -- how can I bring closer the human kind to their problems and to understand better the problems they may have and the -- their manner and the way they live, how they live, how they are as human beings.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And tell me, how does tape recording surreptitiously, without the knowledge or consent of a friend, help you in this regard?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS LL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Just as I tape the lectures when I attend some history classes, for instance, to understand better what was said, just as I take notes openly. Likewise, at a dinner when I cannot take notes because it is impossible for me to eat and take notes at the same time, then it is the customary practice. So I decided, just as I have always done, to record these conversations so as to be able to analyse them subsequently and so that I could understand better what was said. But I do it, then I analyse them subsequently, following the event.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness LL, is this tape recording that you made at the dinner party available, or has it been, unfortunately, lost like the videotape and the still pictures you testified about yesterday?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS LL [Resumed]
utterances.text: When I learned that I would be called by this Tribunal, I did my best to find this tape, to try to establish -- to try to establish contact with the military superiors to whom the tape was given. And unfortunately, I could not find it. But I've undertaken to find it so as to be able to -- and I hope I will be able to offer it to the Tribunal, and I will continue my efforts.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Since you routinely tape-recorded conversations during your term in Bosnia-Herzegovina, can you give me a list of the other military or civilian authorities that you surreptitiously recorded?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Scott.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: I object to that, Your Honour, as to relevance and beyond the scope of direct examination.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Meek. This question is too broad.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: I'll narrow it down.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was Ivan Andabak -- was this the only occasion during your tenure in Bosnia-Herzegovina that you surreptitiously tape-recorded conversations without the knowledge of the people you were taping?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS LL [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you -- can you give me the name or names of some of the other individuals that you tape-recorded conversations without their knowledge? Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Excuse me, Mr. President. For sake of the Spanish government which, of course, would control these decisions, not this witness, I have to invoke Rule 70. And any request to that effect would have to be directed to the Spanish government, which I suggest counsel can do. But this witness cannot make any commitments to turn over documents belonging to the Spanish government or to declassify or otherwise make those documents available.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: Mr. President, may I respond.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Meek.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: This witness has testified extensively about his four months or so in Bosnia-Herzegovina and his activities and the people he spoke with. He declined on direct examination to bring forth the evidence that he had surreptitiously tape-recorded the conversation bearing the voice of my client allegedly, and Mr. Andabak. It's -- the Prosecution has opened the door to these questions. I'm not asking them to turn over the information obviously because I don't know if they have it. All I'm asking for is some names of other people that he may have tape-recorded. If he gives me an answer that yes, he did, then Mr. Scott may be correct, there are ways that we can request those -- that information. However, we can go into closed session, if that would be appropriate. But I cannot know -- I'm not a fortune teller. I have no crystal ball. And therefore, I would not know who to ask -- what tapes to ask for if they are even in existence today unless I know who he taped.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Scott.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Mr. President, to clarify something on this so the record is clear. It was not the witness, and it should not be blamed on the witness, who omitted to testify about the existence or the alleged taping of this dinner conversation. I didn't ask, and because the tape -- the tape is not available, therefore, I didn't inject the issue into the case. I didn't rely on it. I have not sought to rely on it, and that is why it wasn't brought up specifically. In fact, I did not open the door on direct examination because I specifically did not raise any issue about the tape at all. So we continue in our objection, Mr. President. And again, this is beyond the scope. The only question to this witness is about this particular conversation with Mr. Tuta, and it has already been admitted and there has been cross-examination that apparently it was tape-recorded. There is now no dispute that as of this moment, the tape cannot be located. And that's the only thing that's relevant. And whether he tape-recorded a hundred other people during his tour in Bosnia is simply irrelevant to this case.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: May I respond one more time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: No, no, no. We have to stop here. We are not debating these very issues at this moment. We are going to make our ruling. Mr. Meek, we believe that your question is of a nature of fishing which is beyond the scope of this case. You may ask a particular question about whether on other occasions, your client's conversation was taped or not. But you could not ask a broad question for all other occasions because this witness is under the protective measures and with the permission of the Spanish government under the conditions of the State confidentiality. I hope you could skip this question, Mr. Meek.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: I will try another way, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness LL, during your tenure in Bosnia-Hercegovina --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CLARK
utterances.text: Can I interject?

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: Yes, Judge Clark. Please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CLARK
utterances.text: I'm just trying to tease out what you're doing. This witness has given specific evidence that at a dinner party, he gathered a lot of information about Mr. Andabak and your client, who he describes as Mr. Tuta. He says that his information came mainly from Mr. Tuta and was confirmed possibly a few days later by other unnamed sources. Just suppose you continued your line of inquiry and you asked this witness does he have a tape recording of the conversation, if that witness was to say, well, as a matter of fact I do, and I can bring it here on Monday. And we sat and listened to the tape recording of Mr. Tuta telling this witness exactly what he says he said, how would that advance your case? I mean, shouldn't you attack this witness in relation to the conversation that day or the interpretation he put on it, rather than ask to hear the tape recording?

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: Your Honour, to respond, Your Honour, that's a very astute observation. On the other hand, if, for example, this witness had tape-recorded other conversations that would tend to exculpate my client, that would have people indicating that Mr. Tuta was only a civilian, that he had no place in a military organisation, he had no command authority, then in that event, Your Honour, that's exculpatory evidence that I believe that I would have a right to delve into. And I understand, but one other question or point I would like to make is that in the direct examination, as we know, there's no videotape available. There's no still shots available, but yet this was talked about in direct examination. Just because the Prosecutor failed to bring forth the fact that the surreptitious conversation -- or taping of this conversation does not make it beyond the scope of direct examination. If you understand where I'm coming from, perhaps there is exculpatory information that has been taped from other individuals. Maybe not.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CLARK
utterances.text: Mr. Meek, do you remember what the President said to you a few minutes ago? He said that he felt that your line of inquiry was a fishing expedition, and I think you've proved that he is correct, because you're asking a series of questions to which you have no idea what the answer is. You don't know of the existence of any tapes that could possibly be exculpatory, and aren't you going into very deep water when you start asking questions to which you don't know the answer?

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: Always, but --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CLARK
utterances.text: Well, that's what I want to say. I think you should address yourself, Mr. Meek, to the qualitative evidence that we know about rather than --

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: One more question on that issue, and I think it can be answered simply yes or no. Did any of the other people, unnamed, that you may have tape-recorded their conversations, did they ever mention my client, Mr. Tuta, Mr. Naletilic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS LL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Could you please repeat the question? I didn't understand it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, let me try again. I understand that you first learned of the existence of Mr. Tuta at the dinner party at Mr. Andabak's house. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS LL [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So prior to that time, you would have not talked to anybody that would have given you information about Mr. Naletilic; correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS LL [Resumed]
utterances.text: No specific information, that is true.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Subsequent to that time, from your testimony, you spoke with some high-ranking HVO officials who gave you some information regarding Mr. Naletilic. Am I correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS LL [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was after the report was prepared, that is, to -- to the report which was done between -- on the 6th or the 7th of April. That is, on the 7th of April, this report -- that report was drawn up and made only on the basis of the conversation I had with your client and which he personally gave me. Following the 7th of April and until my departure in July, in the area of -- in the zone of operations, there were constantly contacts with the military and civilians of the HVO and the BHA, and in all these contacts, I was trying to collect more information, not only about Mr. Tuta but also about other people and about other events and developments which could affect the performance of our duties.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How many -- how many other profiles, so to speak, did you draft up concerning individuals in Bosnia-Herzegovina aside from Mr. Naletilic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS LL [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is very interesting to know how the military authorities -- how are we? What kind of people are we who are going to interview to, to see how we can help, how we could contribute to the resolution of their problems or their personal difficulties? In other words, with all the people that I talked with, with all these people, I also developed a certain idea, what they are like, what kind of personality they are. I tried to pursue that in order to understand them better, to understand better the problems and the kind of help that I could offer them.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you, Witness LL, but maybe you didn't understand my question. The Exhibit 327 is a profile which you've testified you composed; correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS LL [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't have here the Exhibit 327. Is it the report that I wrote about Mr. Tuta?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS LL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Then yes, not only his profile but all that was said and done at that dinner. And this is the personal profile, yes, about this person, about Mr. Tuta.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you make a profile on Ivan Andabak?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS LL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: To the best of your knowledge and recollection today, approximately how many people - I don't want their names - did you create profiles on?

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Your Honour, I'm going to object at this point.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: I've intentionally given some latitude. I think the question about Mr. Andabak is reasonably within some scope, but now we're going far afield, and I object, and I'm sure the Spanish government would object.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: I quite agree with you. Mr. Meek --

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. I will --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: -- concentrate on your client, please.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness LL, had you read any newspaper articles whatsoever or magazine articles about Mr. Naletilic prior to the dinner party in April 1993?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS LL [Resumed]
utterances.text: You are asking me if I read anything, articles that would refer -- that would be referring to Mr. Naletilic, is that it?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, sir?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS LL [Resumed]
utterances.text: The truth is that I just don't remember. I'm not sure. I don't think so. I don't think I read anything, but I really cannot say yes or no. I don't remember ever registering having read anything about him prior to that event.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Thank you very much. You mentioned in your testimony that you had perhaps spoken with some HVO personnel to help either in the drafting of this profile or in the confirming of this profile within the two days that it took from the dinner party to the completion of the profile. Could you tell me the names of the HVO personnel that you spoke with?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS LL [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. After the dinner party, I did not talk with any person requesting that he or she confirms the information. It was only subsequently, at a later stage. If any change of my impressions that I gained would have happened, then I would have changed the report. But subsequently, the HVO sources practically confirmed all that I had already learned. Had it changed in any way, the picture that I gained, I would have registered that, but nothing like that happened after the 6th or the 7th of April.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Please then give me the name or names of the HVO personnel who you spoke with subsequent to the drafting of this profile.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS LL [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think that in view of the professional secret that exists in the military, we cannot disclose the sources which are confidential sources. These are some rules, and therefore, this is the professional secret, and I do not think I really can name anyone else.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: Mr. President, Your Honours, this puts in me in a dilemma. Obviously, I don't see how anything that he has testified about in this Tribunal can be any longer deemed to be a secret or confidential. He has been allowed to speak about and come here and testify before this lofty Tribunal as to what he did in his operations and during his duties in Bosnia-Herzegovina. If he hypothetically tells me, "I spoke with individual A, B, and I spoke with individual C and D," and we can find those individuals, we may be able to discredit this witness in our case, and by disallowing such a question, hampers a defence and denies us the right to a fair trial and denies us the right to confront the witnesses against us, and I don't think it's fair to claim secret when he has been allowed to testify in this Tribunal about what he did during his tenure in Bosnia-Herzegovina in 1993. Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Meek, you have to understand that this witness comes here --

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Go ahead, Mr. President. I have a comment, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: -- to give the testimony on the conditions that we should not disclose any State secrets of the confidentiality. And in accordance with the Rule 70(D), this Trial Chamber may not compel the witness to answer any questions related to the information and its origin if the witness declines to answer on the ground of the confidentiality which is quite clearly stipulated in the Rules. No matter if you like it or not, you have to abide by this Rule.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: I will abide by your ruling, Your Honours, and I would take exception, for the record for appeal purposes, that I am not being allowed to question this witness on matters that he spoke about on direct examination. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Witness --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Scott.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: As I said, referring to what counsel just said about the record for appeal, let me also make a record. I quite agree with Your Honour, and I was going to say -- and Your Honour is quite correct -- under Rule 70, section (C) and (D), the rules are quite clear about this. The Chamber has had occasion to review those just recently, so I'm not going to just simply refer to them again. As I've indicated, Mr. President, you've already noted that. We would note that further. Counsel is not, in our view, substantially prejudiced in cross-examining this witness. He has the document in front of him. There, indeed, has been extensive cross-examination about the preparation of the document. It has been the subject of cross-examination continuing from yesterday. There has been, we submit, no prejudice to this Defence. They can go into every part of this document. Indeed, I suggest to the Chamber that the time has come on this document for the Defence to squarely put the case to this witness. Are they saying this document is fabricated? Put that to the witness. Are they suggesting that the content of this document -- there hasn't been one question to the content of the document. If there's a statement that they suggest is false, put it to the witness. They have not been prejudiced in this cross-examination largely because the cross-examination has not been proper.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Mr. Meek, you have full right to make an interlocutory appeal concerning the rulings of this Trial Chamber. And please continue your cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness LL, during your tenure in Bosnia-Herzegovina in 1993, did you know an individual by the name of Petkovic, General Petkovic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS LL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you have occasion to speak with General Petkovic specifically about my client, Mr. Naletilic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS LL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I spoke with General Petkovic, and I remember he gave me a card of his own, and he signed it. And he wanted to express his gratitude to me by signing it after a meeting in Medjugorje with Colonel Zorzo. And as regards your client, I had no opportunity of asking General Petkovic anything about him.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: During your tenure in Bosnia-Herzegovina, did you meet a General Lasic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS LL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you meet General Bozic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS LL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you meet General Obradovic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS LL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you meet General Praljak?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS LL [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember. If I could see a photo of the gentleman, I could perhaps answer. Perhaps I did meet him in an interview between commanders. If I could see a photo, it would be easier for me to identify this person. In other words, I don't think I had a personal relationship with this person, but perhaps I did meet him, perhaps during an interview with General Zorzo because many generals came to the conversations that were held regularly in Medjugorje.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you, Witness LL. In regards to the generals that I spoke about, except for General Praljak, did any of the other generals give you any information concerning Mr. Naletilic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS LL [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do remember that I spoke with Mr. Bozic and Mr. Obradovic about many topics, including a general whose name you have not mentioned whose name is in the statement I made earlier and that you sent me yesterday, a military man from the HVO. And I think that in these conversations, the name of your client always came up because he was a man of great influence within the HVO, and I always tried to contrast the information I received, any data, not in a direct fashion, not by speaking about your client only. But in a conversation that lasted several hours, something always came up. And I would always try to find out about details and see if I could confirm information during these conversations.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And in the course of your deployment in Bosnia-Herzegovina, did you have occasion to speak with any military individuals from the ABiH army that might have spoken to you about Mr. Naletilic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS LL [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have heard -- I heard HVO, and here I'm reading ABiH. Which is it, please?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: ABiH.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS LL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes. In exactly the same way as I spoke to commanders of HVO, I spoke to commanders of ABiH. And I spoke to members -- about members of HVO to those of ABiH and the other way around. These people knew each other perfectly well. They belonged to the same army. They had been working together years earlier, they knew each other. And very often, the conversations, the name of your client and the names of other military men would come up.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: To go back to the formal statement that you gave, do you still have that in front of you, Witness LL?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS LL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. The document you sent to me yesterday.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes, LL. That is your formal statement to the Office of the Prosecutor. Could you please turn to page 6. It would be the paragraph below the short paragraph where you stated all the information about Tuta came from Andabak. Could you have your interpreter read that next paragraph to you, please.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS LL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I have read this paragraph.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And Witness LL, is it true that you found it very difficult to place Mr. Naletilic into the organisation of the HVO?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS LL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, you are perfectly right because the first time I saw your client, he was very well dressed, very groomed. He was a civilian. He did not look like a warrior like Hudruk or Ivanov. But it was difficult, therefore, for me to feel that he was a military man, a professional officer, but then I realised that he did belong to that organisation.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, this statement that you gave to the OTP in November of 2000 was based on all of your knowledge up to the date of giving that statement, was it not?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS LL [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, it's not quite correct. There are many things I couldn't remember at the time I made this statement. And as time has passed, I have recalled to date, from the time that statement was made, many other details. One day I was called to make this statement, and I declared what I remembered. And then afterwards, I saw some documents. I refreshed my memory, and I remembered all these conversations, and these details were confirming all the written paragraphs in this statement.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So basically, your memory is getting better as time goes by. Is that your testimony?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS LL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. As we talk about the topic, we are talking about this topic specifically, I remember more and more facts about the experience I lived through because it's the same thing as when you try to remember about something that happened, a specific event, that I hadn't thought about for, let's say, ten years.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you gave your statement in -- a year ago to the Office of the Prosecutor, you said that Tuta did not have any military rank and, in your opinion, did not belong to the HVO organisation at all. Isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS LL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Possibly he was not part of the HVO. In other words, I mean to say that it was very difficult for me to think that he was part of it. Perhaps it's too categoric a statement to say that he did not belong to it, because thanks to all the conversations I had with Ivan Andabak and with other sources, I heard that he was a member of HVO.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: About a year ago, it was your opinion he was not; correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS LL [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, it is not correct. I --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I would ask -- Witness LL, please look at the second sentence in that paragraph. Doesn't that in fact say that, "In my opinion, did he not belong to the HVO organisation at all"?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS LL [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's not exactly what I tried to say. If you're referring to this specific sentence, military rank -- I could not find out about his military rank. You're right. I could never find out exactly which military rank, but I knew that he was there. He appeared, he disappeared, and this is why it's rather confusing or would look a bit confusing. But later on, I realised and I was able to confirm the fact that he did belong to it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Would this be later on, after the statement of November 2000?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS LL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Yes. In this statement, perhaps I was misunderstood, wasn't understood correctly enough. What I tried to say is that he belonged to it, but I couldn't know exactly what rank he had. Perhaps I was speaking Spanish and I wasn't understood correctly. And this is a translation of my statement into English of my statement in Spanish. And later on at home, I looked through papers, and I remember he himself told me that he did belong to the organisation.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you ever observe Mr. Naletilic at any military meetings of a high level?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS LL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. He came to a meeting of the commanders in Medjugorje. In one opportunity, he met with Colonel Zorzo and other commanders as well.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you didn't mention that meeting anywhere in your statement you made last year, did you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS LL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. There are many things I did not say. This statement was drafted. I had so many meetings. It's difficult to give you exact details of every single meeting that -- private meetings with Colonel Morales, Colonel Zorzo. It's difficult for me to give you specific details of the many, many meetings that took place with Mr. Tuta and with other companions of Mr. Tuta, with commanders of the Spanish army. It's difficult in a statement to give you all the details about all meetings.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And that's because you were in attendance and present at many, many meetings during your tenure; correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS LL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And just as you testified it's difficult to remember exact details because of all the meetings you were at when you gave this statement, isn't it equally as difficult to be able to testify about those today?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS LL [Resumed]
utterances.text: If I speak frankly, it's not quite the same thing, because let's say from last year to date, I've looked at all the INTREPs and INTSUMs, and I have been able to have a clear idea of the whole situation after a period of ten years.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you recall the occasion that General Zorzo, when he left to go back to his country, that there was a going-away party in Medjugorje?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS LL [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do not remember.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You were not there at the going-away party for General Zorzo?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS LL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I remember that General Zorzo changed his shirt or T-shirt. He gave away some T-shirts of the Tactical Group, and there was an exchange of T-shirts. It was a multifarious meeting indeed.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But is it your testimony that you don't recall a private dinner party that was held in honour of General Zorzo when he was about to go back home?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS LL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, I do remember this dinner party, and I remember the detail, that General Zorzo put on the T-shirt. You know, he took off his military uniform, and he put on this T-shirt that had been given to -- by somebody else from the Tactical Unit. He was a very open-minded man. He liked this type of thing.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you recall that my client, Mr. Naletilic, was present at that going-away party?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS LL [Resumed]
utterances.text: If I'm sincere, I don't really remember. I don't remember, because there were so many people there. Perhaps he was at that party, but if I'm going to speak up frankly, I don't really see your client there in that dinner party because there were so many guests. It is rather difficult to remember whether he was there or even whether Mr. Andabak was Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. there too. If you tell me the names of the commanders who were there, I would be unable to answer that question.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You say that perhaps he was at that party. And is it true that perhaps this was the incident or meeting which you've referred to when my client, Mr. Naletilic, was in Medjugorje?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS LL [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I know that before there had been another meeting. Not only in this meeting. I'm not referring to this meeting only. Regarding that meeting, I don't remember. There were other meetings where your client was there in meetings with Colonel Zorzo.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, it's my understanding that your testimony to date has been that you observed or saw my client at one meeting in Medjugorje.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Well, Mr. President, I'm going to object.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, Mr. Scott.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: If the Defence counsel continually suggests and indicates to this witness that -- invites him to remember other meetings including where his client was, I don't think there's anything improper with the witness either trying to respond and say, "I either remember additional meetings," on being prompted by counsel's own questions, or saying he doesn't remember, what have you. But for counsel to suggest on the one hand, "Weren't you at this meeting? Weren't you at this meeting?" and then come back and say, "But you say there was only one meeting," it strikes me as unfair. If counsel is suggesting that in fact his client had much more extensive dealings with the Spanish Battalion, I'm not sure that helps his client, but if that's what he wants to suggest, we'll accept that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Mr. Meek, if you said that this witness was at certain meetings, show him your evidence about it. If you have a document saying that this witness was present at such meetings, you have to refresh the witness's memory about it. You cannot ask one meeting after another. You have to put an end to this questioning.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: Mr. President, I certainly would like to express my gratitude for my learned colleague, Mr. Scott, and he is very clever. But the problem is that this witness in his written statement never mentioned any meetings with Mr. Tuta in Medjugorje, and now I am learning about more. So I'll ask this question.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness LL, to the best of your recollection today, how many meetings did you observe Mr. Naletilic attend in Medjugorje at your headquarters?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS LL [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I can remember, I can only remember one meeting only. I can't remember any other meetings apart from the one you have mentioned now, this dinner party. I don't remember that he was there, but before, I do remember that Colonel Zorzo had some meeting with him.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Your Honour, excuse me.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: The record should reflect that is exactly consistent with what this witness has testified. He has never said anything inconsistent.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: Let the record reflect what the record reflects. Thank you, Judge.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, Witness LL, you have described Ivan Andabak as a friend. Am I correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS LL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And in your testimony yesterday, you described the last time that you saw him in Siroki Brijeg in 1997 at his home, did you not?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS LL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you tape-record that conversation also?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS LL [Resumed]
utterances.text: That conversation, I don't think I recorded at all. It was a meeting to say goodbye. I didn't really think it was necessary to make any recording. Because it was the day I was leaving; I was in a hurry. And I do remember that I went to say goodbye to his wife Juani and his daughter, who I really liked. And I don't think I made a recording at all.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know if Mr. Ivan Andabak had any health problems, since you were his friend?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS LL [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think so, but I cannot tell you exactly what type of problem. I don't know whether he had stomach problems or -- as of now, I know that he looked all right. He looked physically fit. But I don't know. He couldn't smoke. He could not eat spicy food. I don't remember exactly what was wrong.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you recall if Mr. Ivan Andabak had a drinking problem?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS LL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Oh, no, I can't remember. At least when he had conversations with me, when I saw him at his home, he always looked calm, collected, and happy. He likes to make jokes, he gets on with everybody. And with me, he never showed me that he had that problem. I never saw him getting drunk.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was that the last time you ever had any contact with Mr. Ivan Andabak, either personally, by phone, or by letter?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS LL [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I saw him. I was able to greet him again when I went back to Bosnia-Herzegovina in 1997.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In 1997, when you returned, did you see him on a regular basis, or was it a single encounter?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS LL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I didn't see him as often as I did during my first mission, because my mission was different. I think I saw him twice or three times at most during the whole length of my mission, because I respected him, and I wanted to express to him that I could help him if necessary. He had built a new home for himself, and he lived there with his wife Juani and with the child.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And since you left Bosnia-Herzegovina during your second mission, have you had any contact with Ivan Andabak?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS LL [Resumed]
utterances.text: After I left Bosnia-Herzegovina, after it is my second mission after 1997, it was the same thing. I said goodbye to him and his family, went back to Spain. And since then, I did not have any contact with Ivan Andabak.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You talked yesterday about the sighting of Ivan Andabak on I believe the 7th of day of May, 1993, near the headquarters in Mostar. Do you recall that testimony?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS LL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you indicated that he was dressed in black. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS LL [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And that he indicated that he was going out on some mission that night. Am I correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS LL [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: This concerned you, so you went back to your command and informed your commander of this situation. Correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS LL [Resumed]
utterances.text: First I went to the BH army headquarters in order to establish the details. And after that, yes, you're quite right.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness LL, you went to the BH army headquarters to tell them that there may be an attack. Isn't that what you did?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS LL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, specifically, I went there to ask them if they knew that something was afoot. And they were the ones who told me that yes, something was going on which their sources had identified, that is, that they were expecting an attack. And then I quickly went to our headquarters.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Your own sources did not have any information about any purported attack, did they?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS LL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, but there was Ivan himself who told me that. And because I could see what he looked like, that he was in full gear and armed, and since I was the only one who he talked with, then I didn't see any reason to look for other sources.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: No attack happened that night, did it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS LL [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct. That night, we did not witness any attack. There was no attack in Mostar -- excuse me, not in the city of Mostar which we were patrolling. I do not know what was the situation elsewhere.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You never observed Mr. Naletilic, my client, in any battles, did you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS LL [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, sir, never.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You never observed my client issuing any orders to anybody, did you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS LL [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, never.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: On the morning of May the 9th, 1993, you were on a hill above Mostar when you encountered one or two buses full of Muslims. Correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS LL [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, no, it is not. There were 20 or 25 busfuls of Muslims.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In your testimony yesterday, I thought you testified that you spoke to a bus driver and stopped a bus and asked where they were going and asked them to stop what they were doing on a hill above Mostar.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS LL [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I didn't speak to the driver but to people in a military vehicle which were moving ahead of the whole -- which led the convoy.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And LL, were there 20 buses in that convoy, or 2?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS LL [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, no, no. There was a convoy with at least 20 or 25 buses. There was a large number of buses and full, full of civilians. I mean, there were buses which were normally part of the urban transport.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: My question is, did you recognise or discover that any of these HVO officers were under the command of Mr. Naletilic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS LL [Resumed]
utterances.text: At the time, it didn't occur to me to ask these things, because the only orders which might come from Mr. Naletilic would come -- this kind of information would come from Mr. Andabak. But it didn't occur to me at the time to ask that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: It's very simply put. You have no evidence, do you, that any of these HVO soldiers manning these buses or convoys were in anyway related to Mr. Naletilic, do you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS LL [Resumed]
utterances.text: The only proof that I have are the HVO sources, but not lieutenant, another source. And, then, yes, I was told that Mr. Naletilic had took part in some battles and that he liked to do that, but nothing, nothing from this lieutenant who was in charge of the convoy which was transporting the prisoners.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: LL, perhaps it's in the translation, but I was asking about that specific incident that you testified about yesterday with the buses, those specific soldiers.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS LL [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did not ask him.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Did you -- and you may not know about this at all, but it's come in prior testimony. There had been an UNPROFOR tank located near the Vranica building in West Mostar. Do you have any knowledge of that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS LL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Impossible. We did not have any tanks in the area. We had APCs, the armoured -- that is, personnel carriers, and they are vehicles using wheels. They do not have any guns. They were not tanks.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You testified yesterday about a drive -- the drive from Mostar area to Citluk and on to Medjugorje on the 9th of May, 1993. Do you recall that testimony?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS LL [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you spoke about encountering some soldiers firing a long gun or Bofors towards Mostar. Do you remember that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS LL [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is right. I was on the road from Mostar to Medjugorje, and there I came across two artillery pieces belonging to the HVO.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you have any evidence that the soldiers manning those guns were under the command of Tuta?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS LL [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did not ask that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You also indicated these guns were pointed towards the headquarters of the BH army in Mostar; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS LL [Resumed]
utterances.text: They were aimed, pointing at Mostar. I do not know. I mean, what? I know the direction, because this is a piece that had a 10 kilometre range. So I do not know exactly. I know the direction. I know that they were firing in the direction of Mostar. And what I also can say, that on the hill, at the time when we were on the hill, we could see that these projectiles were falling, were hitting the Muslim neighbourhood, the Muslim side, but all that I can say is that these guns were pointing at Mostar and that they were being fired. From the place where I was on that elevation, if this has to do with those pieces of artillery on the hill which I saw form the hill, then it is possible that they were hitting that part. But I really cannot say whether the projectiles which were hitting the area which I could see from the hill were coming from these pieces, but when I was at the place where those artillery pieces were, I could not see where exactly these -- what these projectiles were hitting.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Thank you, Witness LL. I think you also testified that these artillery pieces are quite precise. Is that true?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS LL [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is. They have long barrels, and these long-barreled guns tend Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. to be very precise.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And with any such weapon such as a gun or a Bofors, the precision depends on the individual firing those weapons; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS LL [Resumed]
utterances.text: In artillery, it is the ballistic calculations rather than the person. That is, the person who calculates all the target data, that is what matters more than the person who fires the shot himself.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you have no knowledge or information as to how the ballistic calculations were made on the 9th day of May, 1993 with these guns, do you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS LL [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I don't.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: A quick question about these buses with the Muslims. Were the military police there with them?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS LL [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember. I know they were HVO troops because they had the emblem, but I do not remember if they had anything that would identify them as military police. I just don't remember. I remember camouflage uniforms and the HVO insignia, that is, the military insignia.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did I understand your testimony that you actually filmed some of the fighting that day from an outlook overlooking Mostar and some of the shelling of Mostar that morning?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS LL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you estimate, if you can, approximately how many shells do you believe were launched toward Mostar that day?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS LL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Many. I can't really put any figure to that. That would be known to people who were constantly observing Mostar, who were there in the area. Personally, I cannot tell you really. I did not count them. I was simply trying to observe what was going on, and I was mostly concerned with what was happening at the football stadium.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness LL, on a separate occasion, and there's an INSUM report concerning this, on one day in Mostar, your unit estimated 7 to 10.000 shells fell that day. Is that correct? It may not be.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS LL [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know. Yesterday, I saw an INTREP which said 3.000 -- well, it looked a bit too high to me. It could be 800. But to avoid this -- that kind of problem, we had a radar using -- for these mortars in order to estimate the number of impacts in the area. But I really could not give you any exact figure. People who were in the area, they were writing down this kind of detail, and possibly then it was rectified. The figure that I saw might sound exaggerated to me, but I did hear, yes, them speak about these things, and I know there were people who counted that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: As a military man with your experience, can you give me an idea of approximately how many guns, anti-aircraft, Bofor, et cetera, would have been involved in launching that many shells on that day?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS LL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, it could be 12 pieces deployed in the area; and if they kept up fire all day long, then, yes, you could have 800, 1.000 impacts.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And did your units determine at any time that the Bosnian Serbs may have been shelling Mostar during your tenure there in Bosnia-Herzegovina?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS LL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Prior to these attacks, yes, there were. I know there were some Serb attacks. When our convoys passed through the Neretva valley, towards Jablanica, and these attacks came from the border area, towards -- east of Mostar where there was the confrontation line. As for Mostar itself, I do not remember any Serb impacts. I'm not saying that none of this took place. I simply do not know. I know that there were these Serb impacts east of Mostar along the confrontation line, along the road in the Neretva Valley many kilometres away from Mostar. And I do not know -- I do not know if there were any Serb attacks on Mostar.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. From a military perspective, and with your experience as a military man, could you give me an estimate, if you can, of the approximate number of soldiers, HVO soldiers, who would have taken part in the attack on Mostar on the 9th of May, 1993?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS LL [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is very difficult to say, because this is not conventional battle. This is an attack -- there is no front line. There is not a regiment or a brigade. It is people fighting. So it is very difficult to assess the strength. There were some military troops, that is, there were HVO forces there. But I really could not say how many troops were involved in the fighting, in the attack that night or at dawn the next day.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: We want to know the relevance of those questions. And we were reminded by Madam Registrar that you told her that you will spend approximately one hour for the cross-examination today. We have to estimate the time for how long we have to keep a witness here this morning. Could you inform us how long you're going to take for your cross-examination?

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: First, Your Honour, the relevance issue. This case has dealt with units called the Convicts Battalion, and there has been some numbers of how many people belonged to it. My question was, if this military man knew, if he knew, how many total soldiers were taking place, to give the Trial Chamber some perspective, number one. But in regards to how long I would take --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Are you indicating to us that the Convicts Battalion involved in those shellings?

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: No, no, not at all. Absolutely not. Now, as far as the cross-examination goes, Mr. President and Your Honours, I've tried to ask the questions to get a simple answer. This witness is very forthcoming, and he answers in a lengthy way. I believe many of the questions I've tried to ask, if you know, tell me. And after ten lines he says he doesn't know when all he had to say is I don't recall. So I will try to wrap it up, and I will try to be finished before the 11.00 break, Your Honour. It's one of those things.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CLARK
utterances.text: Mr. Meek, are you ever going to come to the point where you actually address this witness on the content of the information which he received from Mr. Andabak on your own client and which was contained in a report? Because that's really essential, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: It is, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I asked you yesterday, Witness LL, whether or not you would agree with me that Ivan Andabak may not have been completely honest and forthcoming with you, just like you weren't honest and forthcoming with him when you secretly tape-recorded his conversations?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS LL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mr. Ivan Andabak, I knew many things which he could not tell me. I could not complete my information about your client basing myself only on what I heard from him. I told you that I was also getting some other very precise details from other sources and a personal friend like Ivan Andabak. And Mr. Andabak, who was a close friend of Mr. Tuta, he could not really tell me all these things. But from other sources --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness LL, I don't mean to cut you off, but the Trial Chamber is impatient with me, and I don't want my head to roll this morning. You've just testified that you drafted this profile of Mr. Naletilic from one dinner party, so you didn't have any corroboration before you wrote that report. Isn't that a fact?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS LL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Indeed.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS LL [Resumed]
utterances.text: And before -- and I did not have to change anything to correct it before my departure, which means that it was all accurate.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you speaking at this party with Mr. Naletilic in Italian? Is this how you communicated with my client?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS LL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, as you know, I do not speak Italian, but Italian and Spanish are very close, so it is easy to understand. So that some of what Mr. Tuta was saying in Italian I could understand. But if I may, I'd like to tell an anecdote about Mr. Tuta. This is something that happened to me yesterday.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness LL, I don't want my head to roll here. I ask a question, and then Mr. Scott can come back and ask any other questions that he wants to on redirect examination. My question was, "Did you speak to him in Italian?" and you answered that question.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS LL [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do not speak Italian, but yesterday Mr. Tuta, at 11.00, before the break, told me a word in Italian, a sentence in Italian which I understood perfectly even though I do not speak that language. That is, we could understand one another. I could understand him, I could listen to him, because there are certain sentences which we can understand.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Witness, you told us that yesterday Mr. Tuta said a sentence, a word to you in Italian. Would you please tell this Trial Chamber what he said to you in Italian, please?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. He said, "Non parlare Italiano," with a perfect Italian accent -- or rather, not perfect accent, that is, but I understood it perfectly. And of course, the two -- there are sentences in Spanish and Italian which are perfectly comprehensible to the other side.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: What does that sentence mean in Italian? What does that mean?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It means, "He does not speak Italian."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So which language did you speak with my client, Mr. Tuta, at this dinner party in?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS LL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, we had an interpreter with us, as I already said, who did it openly. And these interpreters, they were -- and since they were talking and helping Mr. Zorzo, I merely -- I only had to listen what Mr. Tuta was saying. And he was speaking in Croatian and said then some sentences, in order to make us understand, he said some of the things he was saying in Italian.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So basically you were not being -- you were not speaking with Mr. Tuta directly. You were eavesdropping on the conversation he was having with General Zorzo. Would that be a fair statement?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS LL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, that was the normal flow of conversation. There was also cross-exchanges. You know, a sentence would come from here or there, a question would come from another side and that was that, but that is about it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was Mr. Tuta drinking that night, alcohol?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS LL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, well, well, well, naturally one takes alcohol towards the end of the dinner, and it took some time. But at the dinner itself, I do not remember. I really don't.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You spent a lot of time in East Mostar, did you not, LL?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS LL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I tried to devote my time equally to East Mostar as to West Mostar.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you ever visit the Fourth Elementary School in Mostar?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS LL [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Your group, for a while, was in the Konjic area; correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS LL [Resumed]
utterances.text: In Konjic, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And were you -- was your unit there about 23 of March in Orliste, the town of Orliste?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS LL [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't tell you. Orliste is a village near Konjic. Is it there? I just don't know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you recall being in a village in Trusina?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS LL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Personally, no, I don't -- I wasn't. Perhaps my troops were there. Because we went around all the villages and all the towns I may have passed through it, but right now, I just can't remember that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Going back - and I'm about finish - you -- in your official statement to the Office of the Prosecutor, you indicated that all of the information about Tuta came from Andabak, and now you've explained that other sources later on confirmed some information; correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS LL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness LL, would it be a fair statement that approximately 90 per cent of the information about Mr. Tuta came from Ivan Andabak?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS LL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, what I can say, that 90 per cent was also cross-checked with other sources.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But then you'll agree that about 90 per cent came from Ivan Andabak?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS LL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, not exactly. Mr. Tuta was the principal source of information at precisely that dinner party. He's the one who gave me all these details about his business, about his actions, about his plans, and that was the broadest possible information that I obtained at that dinner. And after that, I told you, yes, I tried to have these details corroborated.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And before the break, one last question. And with all that information that you claim you got at this dinner party, you still could not give him a military rank, and in your opinion, did he not even belong to the HVO. Isn't that a fact and isn't that what you told the Office of Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. the Prosecutor one year ago?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS LL [Resumed]
utterances.text: At this dinner party, no, that was not clear to me. I didn't have a clear picture. And after that dinner, it became quite clear that yes, he did belong to the HVO.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But your report was generated within 48 hours of the dinner party; correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS LL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you, Witness LL.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: Might --

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Before anyone rises, and I say this because the observation is important for now, the Chamber may notice -- well, now it's changed. I just want the record to reflect that throughout this testimony, Mr. Naletilic has not been wearing his headphones, has been clearly interacting with this witness in terms of shaking his head, laughing, clearly interacting the way that someone would interact if they understood exactly what this witness was saying in Spanish. He has not been wearing his headphones throughout this time. He's just now picked them up. He has them in his hand now. And he has been clearly interacting with this witness and showed every evidence of knowing exactly what was being said without using to any translation.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: Mr. President, I'm going to have to object to that. Obviously my back has been to my client, and there are cameras all in this courtroom. And I would invite the Trial Chamber to watch the tape. If what Mr. Scott is claiming happened happened, the tape will show it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: I have to send a warning to you and to your client that you should be very careful in this courtroom. Any suggestions given by your client to you, his counsel, might be interpreted differently by the other party or by the witness. Sometimes it will be mistakenly, I must say, as a threat to the witness. So you have to be very careful about the behaviour in this courtroom. And you have the obligation to warn your client. First, your communications between you and your client is fully respected, and it should be conducted in entire confidentiality. Secondly, don't make any gestures which could be possibly mistaken as something else. This is just advice to you.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: Mr. President, have I done anything improper? I have not done anything improper, I don't believe. I don't believe --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: No, it's your obligation to give some advice to your client.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: I will speak with my client, Your Honour. There's no question there.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Mr. Scott, do you think we have to have a break?

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: I think we probably should, Your Honour, but in fairness to counsel, Your Honour, I was not suggesting any improper communication between counsel and his client. I was -- I did mean to intend, and I do mean to intend, that his client was clearly giving all evidence of understanding this testimony without the benefit of translation. And since counsel has made a major issue of his language abilities, I think it's quite pertinent. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Witness, I have to tell you that, as I did to other witnesses, please do not speak to anybody about your evidence during the break and do not let anybody speak to you about it.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: For the record, before we break, it has been too long, Your Honour. But I can tell you that I can put my headphones like this, and I can turn the volume up, and I can hear exactly what's being said without having those earphones on my ear, for the record. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: It is in the record already. We have to break. We'll resume at 11.35.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Meek. I assume that you're finished with this cross-examination within the time frame that you promised us.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: Your Honour, one administrative matter. Back on Wednesday, the 7th of November, there was an objection by Mr. Naletilic and from our Defence for Exhibits 508, 595.1, and 612. I would like to formally now withdraw those objections to the admission of those three documents that were tendered on the 7th of November during Witness JJ's testimony. I'm sorry I didn't tell you this yesterday. It slipped my mind, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you very much for your cooperation.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: And I only have two questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, please.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness JJ [sic], it is apparent that during your mission in Bosnia-Herzegovina in 1993, you were talking to a lot of people and asking a lot of questions and gaining a lot of information from many sources, and it was openly known. Would you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS LL [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Will you allow, Witness LL, that during this wartime, during this civil war that was going on in Bosnia-Herzegovina, that the people giving you this information were, in fact, feeding you disinformation to confuse the entire situation and so that you would report back to your superiors with information that was not correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS LL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, speaking for myself, I do not believe that this is correct. The information, which was open information -- and at that time, it was impossible to find out about all details, and to consider it as just a flow of information. It was rather a normal conversation, and it was a contrast operation taking place afterwards thanks to information from different sources, and then there was a written statement. Now, in the case that there was some mistake, automatically, I changed my written statement to my written reports. But in most instances, after I had conversations or -- with all sources, normally always most of the actions that were mentioned by the sources, whether openly or not, took place.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: I have no further questions, Mr. President, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Witness LL, for your forthcoming in this Tribunal.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Seric, cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, Mr. Meek has asked almost all the questions relevant to this Defence. I will have only one question to ask of this witness. Cross-examined by Mr. Seric:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Sir, you are an educated man, I believe, a man of authority, militarily speaking. Could you agree with me when I say that in every war, as in every war, in this war there is also a war of disinformation?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS LL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I agree with you. The war of disinformation always take place, and we have to fight this trend, and we have to try and find out what is wrong, because if not, we would not be working professionally as military men, and this is our job.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you very much. The answer could have been even much shorter.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I do not have any other questions, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Re-examination, Mr. Scott?

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. I have a few questions. Re-examined by Mr. Scott:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness LL, I asked you this in direct examination, but in light of the cross-examination, I will give you the opportunity to respond to it again. Sir, is it correct that it was your specific mission, that is, your professional military assignment during your tour in Bosnia in 1993 to gather as much information as you could, and such information might broadly be called -- what people might call intelligence?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS LL [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. It's not exactly intelligence. It's information. Intelligence is something that is carried out by a special team, and what we wanted to get was information. Later on, there was intelligence organised from other quarters, but I was looking for information.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you, Witness. I think that indicates there may be a difference between what many non-military people might think of in those terms, the difference between gathering information and gathering intelligence. But clearly, your mention was to gather, indeed, as much information as possible?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS LL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. There were other teams carrying out this gathering of information -- of intelligence, and if they had something interesting they had found out about, they would let us know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, Witness, if you have your statement in front of you. I realise it's in English, but perhaps either the interpreter there beside you can assist you, or if you can look at page 7 of the statement, you can at least recognise the names that I will mention to you in the next moment or two. Counsel suggested to you in his questions that the interview that had been conducted of you back in November of 2000 was very specifically focused on Mr. Naletilic. Let me ask then, can you please confirm, looking after your statement, were you also in fact questioned about Mr. Petkovic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS LL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you also asked questions and did you also give information about a Muslim named Zuti?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS LL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You were asked questions about a man named Obradovic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS LL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You were asked questions about the following places which we have not focused on primarily in your testimony here: Dretelj, Gabela; is that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS LL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You were asked about Ljubuski?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS LL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You were asked about another camp called Vojno?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS LL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You were asked about this man Praljak?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS LL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You were asked about a man named Prlic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS LL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: About a man named Coric?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS LL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And a man named Roso?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS LL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. A number of questions were put to me, and I answered the questions as far as my knowledge would allow me to.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, there has been extensive questions to you about this man Andabak. Can you tell the Chamber, by every indication, did it appear that Mr. Andabak and Mr. Naletilic were very close friends? Not merely military associates but indeed close personal friends, as far as you could see and what you heard?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS LL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I was able to assess that they were really very good friends, and they trusted one another.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Tell the Chamber this, if you can: Did you have the impression that Mr. Andabak was proud of being such a close friend of this man named Tuta?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS LL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you think -- did you observe anything that caused you to think that when Mr. Andabak at various moments was giving you information, that he was lying to you and giving you information for the purpose of hurting his very good friend Mr. Naletilic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS LL [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, on the contrary. At times I knew that he felt proud to tell me, and this I have already stated before, the many meetings that they had had together in some combat areas.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Let me ask you, and if I can direct the courtroom's attention, please, to Exhibit P327, the report about Mr. Naletilic, a couple of questions. Now, on cross-examination, the fact that you had tape-recorded this dinner conversation came up. So that having been raised, let me ask you this question: When you prepared your memorandum or report on Mr. Naletilic which has been marked as P327, did you have a tape recording available to you for purposes of preparing your report and, indeed, checking your report for accuracy against that tape recording?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS LL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I had to do this in order to see which were the key ideas that I had gathered during my trip and at night in my own office and in Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. order to confirm in detail all this information here. Because if not, I would not have been able to give so many details.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: On this document, if you can assist us -- you do not speak any Croatian. Is that correct, sir?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS LL [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How, for instance, did you come to know -- on the top of the first page up in the upper right portion of the first page, nickname, it says Tuta, which has been translated -- I'm saying the explanation, the parenthetical, says "child speak for chamber pot". How did you find out that this nickname for Tuta meant chamber pot?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS LL [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think I remember that it was something that was told us by Mr. Tuta himself during the dinner party to Colonel Zorzo and myself. Somebody asked him, What does Tuta mean? And he explained.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: There's also another piece of information. I just point out for whatever assistance it might be to the Chamber. On the top of the page, and probably for these purposes, it's just as well to look at the Spanish version because the translation is not going to be important. I indicate that to the Chamber as well.
