On the top of the first page of your report, do you see something that we recognise as fax information line?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS LL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, this is correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: This would indicate that this report presumably must have existed at least by the 22nd of April, 1993 at 14.15 hours because it was faxed. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS LL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, this is correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The attack on Mostar on the 9th of May, counsel asked you about that -- for that matter, as I did. Did you in your observations that day -- and you've told us how you moved around from the hill on Mostar to an area near Citluk and a number of areas. Can you tell the Chamber, did you see a number of components, multiple components, of HVO forces engaged in the attack on Mostar on the 9th of May?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS LL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Is it in the surroundings of the city of Mostar? Is it outside the city? If it is, I know that there was movement of vehicles from the HQ up to Mostar, from Citluk. There was a lot of convoys and military vehicles moving towards the city of Mostar. Now, inside Mostar, I cannot give you any detailed information on the forces involved because I could not enter the city.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You correctly understand my question. My question is not limited to inside the, if you will, the core city of Mostar. But including the surrounding region, did you see multiple components of the HVO involved in action that day directed toward Mostar?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS LL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, against Mostar -- I know they were moving towards Mostar. There were convoys moving towards the city, but I don't know whether they were going to attack Mostar. They were preparing, militarily speaking, but I did not see any other weapons other than the ones I mentioned in my statement. Perhaps they did, but I personally did not see them.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness LL, forgive me. I'm sure that I'm not putting the questions to you as well as I should. What you have already told us about, if I can remind you, both on direct and in cross-examination, you made certain observations from the hill overlooking Mostar itself. You saw actions taking place, you saw shells impacting in the city of Mostar. Correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS LL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You saw the two other large artillery pieces that were firing at some long range in the direction of Mostar.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS LL [Resumed]
utterances.text: What I saw is two artillery pieces. They were anti-aircraft fire weapons with direct shooting towards the HQ too. Now, as far as mortar is concerned, we could see the explosions, but we did not know where the shooting was coming from. I felt that they came from the west area of Mostar. We could hear the guns, but we did not know exactly where the fire originated, and I did not have freedom of movement at that point. But I did note that there were two anti-aircraft machine-guns shooting against the buildings of the HVO [as interpreted] and against the east side of Mostar, against other buildings there too.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Well, let's pick up with that then. We have the observations on the hill. We have the anti-aircraft fire. Did you not also tell us about seeing two other larger artillery pieces also firing in the direction of Mostar?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS LL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. The two artillery pieces are the ones I saw on the road from Mostar and Medjugorje, in the Citluk area. These are the two artillery pieces I mentioned earlier, and I saw that they were shooting. As I got closer, I saw they were shooting.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: My question to you, and I'm sorry it took so long to lay the foundation, but you are a professional military officer. Can you assist the Chamber in telling how much would it take and what would be required to coordinate military action on that scale?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS LL [Resumed]
utterances.text: It needs perfect coordination, because you have artillery pieces shooting. You have to have a command post as well. You have to have observers that are able to correct the fire from the artillery pieces, and you need trucks with ammunition. You need a lot of ammunition in order to serve the different weapons that are shooting.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Excuse me, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Mr. President, it's been alerted to me that on page 45, line 9, it says that the machine-guns -- "anti-aircraft, machine-guns shooting against the buildings of the HVO," and I think that's a translation or a transcription error. I can ask the witness, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was the fire being directed at the buildings of the HVO or buildings of the ABiH?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS LL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Against the buildings of the Armija, the ABiH and the eastern side of Mostar, the Muslim side of Mostar.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, directing you to your statement. Do you still have your statement in front of you, sir? And I'm going to direct your attention to page 7, the same paragraph. I'm sorry. My mistake. Page 6. The same paragraph that counsel for Mr. Naletilic took you to, but I want you to read the full paragraph with one omission that I'm going to make. MR. SCOTT and so there is no question about this, Mr. President, I'm going to omit one short sentence because -- as an accommodation to counsel, because I think they might view that as being unduly prejudicial. I will simply omit it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you have that in front of you, sir?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS LL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Because of the language difference, I'm going to read it to you, and would you please answer me? Is this what you said in your statement further to what counsel asked you: "It is very difficult to place Tuta into the organisation of HVO. He had not any military rank, and in my opinion," as put here, and you've already indicated you have some questions about this, but I'm simply referring you to this statement, "and in my opinion, he did not belong to the HVO organisation at all." The next sentence says: "He was much more." And now I'm going to omit one sentence. If counsel wishes to raise it, I will leave it in their hands. "He told me in Siroki Brijeg, when I first saw him, that he had come from abroad with a lot of money to help Croats. I think that his original mission was not to take part in fighting, but because he liked fighting, he took part in the fighting as well. Andabak told me that sometimes Tuta was addressed as `Force Commander.' He told me that -- when I asked him, `Who is your boss?' and Andabak told me that it was Tuta. He told me this on many occasions." Now, sir, is that the full statement of the paragraph that you gave in November 2000?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS LL [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is right.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And my final two questions. Going back to Exhibit 327, the report on Mr. Tuta. Directing your attention to that part of your report that says "Current Situation." Was it stated during the dinner conversation that evening that, as you report here: "Tuta receives direct orders from Petkovic and is at the same level of command as Lasic or higher"?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS LL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: My last question to you in that document. If you go to page 2, about the middle of the page in the English version, and I'll see if I can find it in the Spanish version as well. There is a section on the -- it will be on the top of the second page of the Spanish document, toward the -- several lines down from the top. Can you find the words -- can you find the words "Gornji Vakuf." Do you see that? The top of the second page of the Spanish translation.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS LL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: It says -- and then I'll ask you a question. It says, as he himself says, he took no prisoners during the attack on Gornji Vakuf, killing even women and children. Now, sir, do you think you were being provided disinformation about that?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Meek.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: Your Honour, I don't believe Gornji Vakuf is within the scope of this indictment whatsoever. So there's no relevance to it, there's no probative value. It's only brought in to prejudice Mr. Naletilic. It's not in the indictment. Mr. Scott knows it. I object.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Was this matter mentioned during the cross-examination?

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Mr. President, there was extensive cross-examination by counsel for Naletilic, and even by the one question by Mr. Seric, that do people in wartime engage in disinformation? And presumably the effort-- there's going to be an effort to suggest that much of this is based on disinformation. I simply picked out one part of this report. We could go -- we could pick many others, and the Chamber can pick its own. And my question to the counsel is -- or to the witness is, did he think he was being provided disinformation when, according to this document, Tuta himself said he took no prisoners? Was that disinformation or not?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Mr. Meek.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: Your Honours, if that's the point of Mr. Scott's question, I believe this witness has already testified that he didn't believe anybody gave him disinformation. But still, this issue of Gornji Vakuf is outside the scope of this indictment, and it's only being brought forth in the testimony to prejudice my client and has no probative value for what we're here to find.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Mr. Scott, we've got this document at our hands. We could read it ourselves. Can you skip this question.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Yes, I'll skip that question, Your Honour. And let me ask one final question, then, about that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The information that you collected during the dinner conversation that evening, Witness LL, did you believe at that time that Mr. Naletilic was giving you disinformation?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS LL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, in view of that trust which was developing, and since this was the first time that we had met, and because he liked very much the Spanish troops and people who were there, it sounded to me like truthful information. I always tried to crosscheck this kind of information so as not to fall into the trap of disinformation. But I did that after this report was done.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Thank you, Witness LL. I have no further questions, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Any questions from the Judges? Judge Clark, please. Questioned by the Court:

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CLARK
utterances.text: Witness LL, I just have one question. It may lead to another one, but basically I have one question. In the period of time that you became acquainted with Mr. Ivan Andabak and you were aware of his close relationship with his friend Mr. Tuta, did you ever receive any information in relation to whether either Mr. Andabak or Mr. Tuta were paid by anybody for their services, or did they bring their own funds to the cause?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS LL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I don't remember receiving any information prior to my meeting Tuta. What I do know regarding the funds, as Mr. Tuta himself told me, he had invested all his money in this cause. I do not know if from -- there were some money coming from another country to this country at war. There were very many vehicles for military commanders. And there was a country at war. And I guess that some other country could Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. logistically support the HVO. I would say that a country at war does not have very many economic resources.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CLARK
utterances.text: Are you saying that Mr. Tuta told you that he purchased many of these vehicles for the HVO?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS LL [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, no, no. Absolutely no. Mr. Tuta never said anything like that. What he was saying was that the HVO militaries were getting cars for moving around. He did not say where from. All that Mr. Tuta told me was that he had invested a great deal of money in this fall for that cause because he believed he was defending that cause, the cause that he was fighting for. And I can't really say more about the financing, about the economic aspect.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CLARK
utterances.text: Did the same situation pertain to Mr. Andabak?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS LL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, precisely. Absolutely the same thing, the same situation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CLARK
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you. Judge Diarra.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DIARRA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. President. Witness, you were told "We do not like the presence of Muslims". Now, first, under what circumstances were you told that, and who was that who told you that? And did this mean the presence of Muslims in the city of Mostar or throughout Herceg-Bosna?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS LL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Specifically that night of the dinner party, both Mr. Tuta and Mr. Ivan Andabak said that they were against Muslims in that city. And subsequently, later on when talking to other brigade commanders with whom I had contact, like, for instance, Tomic, who was the commander of a brigade at Ljubuski, I think he was also a partisan of that view, that there should be no Muslims in that area.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DIARRA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The city of Mostar and all of the parts of Herceg-Bosna, all over Herceg-Bosna?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS LL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not only the city of Mostar, because it is very difficult to find a Muslim family in Ljubuski or in the interior. Perhaps there are people like that -- perhaps there still are some people.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DIARRA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And my second question: On those rare occasions that you met with Mr. Naletilic, was he wearing civilian or military clothes?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS LL [Resumed]
utterances.text: At the dinner party, he was in civilian. He had a jacket and a tie. On the other occasion, when I saw him in Siroki Brijeg, he was in a military uniform. And on other occasions, I don't remember because that was very sporadic. I do not remember. I remember on those two occasions, specifically on one of them, he was in civilian; and on another one, he was in a military uniform.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DIARRA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much, Witness. I do not have any other questions. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Judge Diarra. Any questions out of the Judges' questions?

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: No, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you. Yes, Mr. Meek.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. Further cross-examination by Mr. Meek:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness LL, you just answered Judge Clark's question about Mr. Tuta taking all of his money and funding in some manner this effort in Bosnia-Herzegovina. Can you tell me what you did to corroborate this supposed statement that Tuta made to you at this dinner party? What did you do?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS LL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I could not ask openly where it came from. I know that he was a very powerful man who fought for the cause, but it was through Ivan Andabak and through -- and other sources also told me not about the amount of money but the effort that this person was investing in supporting the cause.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: That would be the only question I would have from the Judges' questions, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Witness, thank you very much for helping us by giving your evidence. I have to apologise to you for having kept you for so long. When the usher pulls down the blinds, he will show you out of the room. At this stage, this Trial Chamber would also like to express our thanks to the Spanish government for allowing you to appear in this case. We also thank the interpreters, both in the courtroom and in the booth, for their valuable assistance. Thank you very much. We wish you good luck.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: At this stage, are there any documents to tender? Mr. Meek?

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: Your Honour, we would ask that D1/33, which was the former P2 exhibit which this witness marked on, be admitted. And we would also ask that we -- we be given a number for the statement that Witness LL made to the Office of the Prosecutor on 11 of -- excuse me, the November the 3rd of 2000, which this witness testified extensively about and from. And I have more copies than are necessary.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you. Any objections?

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Your Honour, as to the interview statement, as you know, we maintain our same position, that it's not -- the statement itself is not evidence; the testimony is evidence. As to -- well, I'll leave it at that. I will address the Prosecution exhibits.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: How about D1/33, which is about a map that was marked by the witness?

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Assuming we finally got the correct map, no objection.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes. This D1/33 will be admitted into evidence, as well as the three other documents which were mentioned by Mr. Meek at the beginning of this sitting, that is, P508, P595.1, and P612 will be admitted into evidence. Madam Registrar will give those documents proper numbers.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: So they are Exhibit PP508, PP595.1, PP612, and D1/33, and they are exhibits.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Mr. Scott, any documents to tender at this stage?

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Your Honour, I believe they were all previously tendered through other witnesses, including Mr. Aguirre and Mr. Prlic and others. If the Court would just allow me the possibility of double-checking that one last time, but I believe there was nothing tendered or used with the witness that had not been previously tendered.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Meek.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: Just a number for the statement which I indicated I would like to admit, that this witness extensively testified from and about and was given to the Office of the Prosecutor on November 3, 2000.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, at this stage, we can only give it an ID number.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: Yes, an ID number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: ID number will be D1/34.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: Madam Registrar, how many copies would you like?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: For the Chamber, we need six copies and then for the interpreters -- then all these copies for the interpreters. So six copies, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, shall we have the next witness at this stage?

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. Mr. Bos would continue. Actually, he doesn't have to do the direct examination, it was concluded, but he will be handling, if you will, for cross-examination purposes the continuation of the prior witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Usher, could you please bring in the next witness? I guess you have to pull the blinds down again.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honour, the next one is KK, who actually came with the voice distortion. So may I please ask for ten minutes' break.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: That is correct. Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, we'll have a short break. We will resume at 12.30. --- Break taken at 12.20 p.m.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, cross-examination, Mr. Par, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour. Cross-examined by Mr. Par:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, I'm lawyer Zelimir Par. I am one of the Defence counsel for Vinko Martinovic, Stela, and I will put to you several questions, not difficult questions, regarding the conditions of your detainment within the unit about which you testified a few days ago. We'll start with September 1993 when soldiers drove you out of your apartment and brought you to what you called Stela's headquarters. I would like to know, have you observed or deduced from the conversations of the soldiers that their intention was to expel you to the other side of the town? Did you hear the soldiers say anything like that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS KK [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Would you tell me, please, do you remember, was there shooting around the demarcation line on that day? Was it possible on that day to cross the demarcation line without putting your life in danger? Do you remember?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS KK [Resumed]
utterances.text: I wasn't near the line.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But did you hear shooting during that day while you were with those soldiers?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS KK [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Would you tell me, please, on that day after you were driven out of your apartment, did you have any opportunity at all to go anywhere else considering that you were expelled? And was it possible, for instance, to go to the other side if those soldiers had not been keeping you in detention?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS KK [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did Stela ever ask you if you had anywhere else to go to find shelter or accommodation in that western part of the town?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS KK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, he did ask, but we had nowhere to go.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Generally speaking, did he know about your entire situation, about your father having been arrested and taken to the camp? Did Stela know your personal life story?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS KK [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't think he did.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Would you tell me, now, while you were at Stela's quarters, were you guarded? Were you constantly under control in terms of movement?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS KK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Nobody was controlling really. We could move around.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you or your brother have occasion to go to that shop which was nearby to get some groceries for the unit or otherwise?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS KK [Resumed]
utterances.text: There was a shop nearby where we could go buy cigarettes if we had the money.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you being guarded at the time, or would you just go on your own and come back?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS KK [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was very close by.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And where did you get the money to do that shopping?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS KK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, it was some money that we had managed to keep, 10 or 15 deutschemarks.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you tell me about those conditions a little. How did they feed you, what kind of meals you had there, how many a day? Were you starving?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS KK [Resumed]
utterances.text: We had two meals, and we were not starving.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you, perhaps, get any cigarettes there, like the soldiers did?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS KK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Sometimes somebody would give us a pack.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Regarding other conditions, did you have enough water? Did you have normal access to the lavatories? Was it possible for you to keep clean?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS KK [Resumed]
utterances.text: We were allowed to go to the lavatory. And sometimes, if we had time, we could even bathe.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How did you sleep? What were the conditions in the place where you spent the night? Could you describe that room and the conditions in which you slept.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS KK [Resumed]
utterances.text: There were sponge mattresses and some kind of bunk or bed. We could lie down and cover ourselves.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was it possible for you to be constantly with your younger brother, and were the conditions the same for him? Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS KK [Resumed]
utterances.text: For the most part, I was with my younger brother.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Let us move on to that line where you said you occasionally went to work. To begin with, would you please look again at this map that we used the last time. It is Prosecution's Exhibit 14.5. And if there is no clean copy left, I have this one ready to hand to the witness. Witness, you are familiar with this photograph? At the Prosecutor's request, you drew the lines around that zone where you went to work. Would you kindly do that again on this map, because I have some additional questions to ask.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Par, is that the same photo shown by the Prosecutor? We have to make sure about that. What is the number of that photo?

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That is photograph 14.5, the same photograph that Mr. Bos used in direct examination, in examination-in-chief. Perhaps we could put it on the ELMO so that it is visible to everyone. If you would kindly turn on the ELMO.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Mr. Bos.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: I'm just wondering why could we not use that same photograph. He already marked the area. I don't see the relevance of having him mark the area again. Maybe we can use the same photograph.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: We have the same doubts in our mind.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I didn't want him to mark anything on the Prosecutor's -- on what is already the Prosecutor's exhibit, but if the Prosecutor agrees with additional markings being made on his exhibit, then I have no objection to that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: So you are going to ask the witness to make the different marks; right? Thank you. You may use your own photos.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: I do not have an objection if the same photograph is used which has already been marked in the examination-in-chief. It seems easier.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, for the purpose of the filing of the evidence, if the Defence counsel asks the witness to have different markings on that map, we better have a different one.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: Very well, Your Honour. As long as he's not been asked again to mark the area where he worked, because that's already been done on our photograph.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: That's what we understand.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, Witness, would you please mark again the area to which you went to work?

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: Sorry, Your Honours, to interrupt again, but I've just been told that I used Exhibit number 14.4, and this is Exhibit 14.5. So it is a different photograph, and I just want to make -- I thought it was the same photograph, but it isn't.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes. I was just informed by Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I apologise. Then let us take this photograph off the ELMO and let us use photograph 14.4, as suggested by Mr. Bos.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Do you have a clean copy with you?

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Since Mr. Bos agreed to additional markings being made on that photograph, we can use the photograph that was marked earlier.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: So that was the P14.4/2. That was the ID number of this document.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, please look at this photograph and have it put on the ELMO so that we can all remember what this photograph is. Perhaps lower it a little. Witness, what you marked in blue is then the zone to which you used to go. Were there sacks with sand put up anywhere in this area? Could you mark the locations if so?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS KK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, there were sacks with sand.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you show us exactly where and mark it in a different colour, for instance, green? Could you mark the positions of these sacks?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS KK [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now I would like to ask you about those sandbags. Did you notice then that above those sandbags, for the purpose of protection from sniper fire, to obstruct visibility, there are additional things like curtains, canvas sheets, et cetera, to obstruct visibility?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS KK [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't notice any canvas sheet above the sandbags.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And since you were working in this area on this building, could you mark the building, and then I will ask you if you worked in front of that building, behind that building, or inside that building when you were there.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS KK [Resumed]
utterances.text: We worked in this building here and inside here.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you please put it on the ELMO, show us the photograph, and then tell us whether it was in front, behind, or inside that building when you went on your expeditions. Please show with the pointer. If you don't have the pointer, use the marker.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS KK [Resumed]
utterances.text: We worked in this building and in this one.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did I understand you correctly? Inside the building, not in front of it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS KK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Inside.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: While this photograph is still in front of us, could you tell us what units there were outside this area? Do you know of a single unit which was on the border or outside this zone that you marked here? What were their names?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS KK [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know those units.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can we agree then that there were other units alongside this area?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS KK [Resumed]
utterances.text: They existed but I don't know them.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And they were completely different to the unit where you spent several months?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS KK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Just one more question, please. This unit where you spent time with at Stela's, did it go somewhere and was replaced by a different unit or did it spend its -- that entire time there?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS KK [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I know, it was there the entire time, the same unit.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: No further questions.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't know how we will mark this, whether it will be the Prosecutor's exhibit or the joint Prosecutor and Defence Exhibit, or perhaps the Trial Chamber can suggest a solution.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: I believe this photo should be double numbered. I mean, one photo with two numbers. Any cross-examination, Mr. Meek?

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: I'm happy to announce I have none, Your Honours. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Re-examination?

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: Just a very few questions, Your Honour. Re-examined by Mr. Bos:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness KK, when you would sleep in Vinko Skrobo -- sorry. When you would stay in Stela's headquarters and stay there overnight, would there be guards in the headquarters?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS KK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, there were guards.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And how many?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS KK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, about two or three men.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Would they be there every night?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS KK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, there were.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: That's it for my questions to the witness. And maybe, in answer to the question Judge Clark raised on the patch, the person -- the face on the patch, I don't know if I can answer that question now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: I did inquire and, unfortunately, I did not find out who that person is. But what I could say in general is that patches of ATG units would usually be -- the names of the ATG units would usually be combat soldiers who had died in combat. So an ATG name would be a name of a soldier who had died in combat. And unfortunately, we didn't find out whether this Vinko Skrobo was also the name of a soldier in combat. But if it was, it could be that the face was the person of Vinko Skrobo. But I can't be 100 percent sure about that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Witness, thank you very much for helping us by giving your evidence. When the usher pulls down the blinds, he will take you out of the room. At this stage, are there any more documents to tender into the evidence, Mr. Bos?

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: Only this exhibit, which I think we'll get two numbers. But I think it would have been 14.4/2, if I remember well. So we would tender that exhibit.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Madam Registrar will give a proper number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: It's PP14.4/2. And the ID number for the Defence with the same document will be D2/16.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Mr. Par, I suppose you are going to tender that same photograph?

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That is correct. I tender the same thing. And I have no other proposals. So for once, we have a joint suggestion, joint proposal.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you. Madam Registrar will give another number for the same photograph.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That would be D2/16.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Yes, Mr. Meek.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: The Defence of Mr. Naletilic has no objection to those exhibits, Your Honour, for the record.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you. Thank you very much. At this stage the Trial Chamber would like to remind both parties that during the testimony of a witness, that there should be no approach -- no attempt to talk to the witness in any way, no matter in this courtroom or outside this courtroom, by anybody. We do not like to see a witness contaminated during their stay here in The Hague. This warning applies to both parties. Yes, Mr. Scott. What are you going to suggest to this Trial Chamber?

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Mr. President, we have a moment, and I think it might be a good use of time. We can still hopefully finish before 1.00 even. Two things: We wanted to, again, we were going to provide the full tape -- remember the tape, the Vranica tape that Judge Clark had inquired about. We raised that the other day, and we didn't have time to do it then. But today, we might have sufficient flexibility in our schedule a bit to do that. What we're going to do now is over the lunch hour, we're going to provide that to the Defence, and they can make inquiry. There is an abbreviated transcript -- English transcription of what's on the tape. And they can review that. And if the Chamber wishes to review that -- we weren't sure what the Chamber wishes to do. If you want to play that in the courtroom, we can do that. I need to alert the Chamber that I mentioned there was a brief interview that was in between the two parts of the tape that had been played in the courtroom which was not on the original tape. I alert the Chamber, and particularly Defence counsel, to that. It is an interview which I did not know until a few minutes ago, of -- the interview is of Zeljko Bosnjak. It is a very short item, but that have some significance to Mr. Naletilic, in particular. So I want to alert counsel to that and the Chamber, and that it was not in the original tape. And we can either submit it separately or, for these purposes, it can be removed. But I'll provide the tape again to counsel during the lunch hour. The second item, Your Honour, procedural item, is as the Court will recall, there are approximately ten transcripts that have previously been admitted from other cases. There are also a substantial volume of exhibits that are connected to those transcripts, and we wish to tender those today. They are -- I say "tender"; what I should say is make them of record in the case, perhaps. Because by prior Court orders, they have already been admitted.
